title: Every letter git status can print, and what it means
summary: `MM`, ` D`, `A `, `??`, `UU`, `R ` — the two-column short format is the densest information git gives you. Produce each code deliberately and learn to read the whole thing at a glance.
mental_model: Every line is `XY path`. X is what the INDEX says versus the last commit; Y is what your DISK says versus the index. Read left-to-right as 'staged, then unstaged' and every code explains itself.

commit.message: Add files in every state we are about to break

steps.title: A clean tree prints nothing
steps.why: Silence is the base case, and worth seeing once. `-sb` adds a branch line even when there is nothing else to say.
steps.expect: One branch line and nothing else.

steps.title: Produce a modification in each column
steps.why: Three files, three states: staged only, unstaged only, and both. The two-column format is the only view that distinguishes them — `git status` in long form buries it in prose.
steps.expect: M  staged-mod.py, ' M' unstaged-mod.py, MM both-mod.py.

verify.label: the three modification states are distinguishable
verify.hint: X is the index, Y is the working tree

steps.title: Additions, deletions and the difference between them
steps.why: `A ` is a new file staged. `D ` is a deletion staged. ` D` is a file you deleted on disk without telling git — which is why it still shows in `git ls-files`.
steps.expect: A  brand-new.py, D  to-delete.py, ' D' to-delete-on-disk.py.

verify.label: staged add, staged delete and unstaged delete each have their own code

steps.title: Renames only appear once staged
steps.why: `R ` shows a rename with both paths. Git infers it by comparing content, and only after the change is staged — before that you see a delete and an untracked file.

verify.label: a staged rename shows as R with both paths

steps.title: Untracked and ignored
steps.why: `??` means git has never been told about the file. Ignored files are hidden entirely unless you ask — which is why a file matching .gitignore looks identical to one that does not exist.
steps.expect: ?? scratch.txt in both; !! debug.log only with --ignored.

verify.label: …and ignored files do not show at all by default

steps.title: The conflict codes
steps.why: During a merge, `U` appears in one or both columns. `UU` is both-modified, `DU` deleted-by-us, `AA` both-added. These are the only codes where the two columns are not 'staged, unstaged' — they are 'ours, theirs'.

actions.run: git stash push -u -q -m "park the demo states"

steps.expect: AA shared.py — both sides added the same path.

verify.label: a conflict shows a U or AA code
verify.hint: U in either column means unmerged

steps.title: The machine-readable format
steps.why: `--porcelain=v1` is the stable two-column format for scripts. `v2` adds the object ids and modes on each line — everything a tool needs without running four more commands.
steps.expect: v1 compact, v2 verbose with shas and modes.

verify.label: v2 includes branch headers for scripts

steps.title: Read the branch line
steps.why: `-sb` prints `## main...origin/main [ahead 1, behind 2]`. Three facts — your branch, its upstream, and how far apart they are — in one line, and the answer to most 'why can I not push' questions.
steps.expect: The branch line, with no upstream configured here.

steps.title: Commit the demo and check it is clean
steps.why: Every state you produced is now visible in one screen. Learning to scan this instead of reading the long form is the single biggest speed-up in day-to-day git.

verify.label: everything is committed and the tree is clean
…except the ignored file, which is exactly where it should be
the ignored file is still ignored
three commits: the setup, the conflict demo and the cleanup

pitfalls: The space matters. `M ` (staged) and ` M` (unstaged) differ only in position, and in a terminal they look almost identical — this is why `MM` surprises people.
A deleted file shows ` D` until you stage the deletion. `git add -A` or `git rm` stages it; `git add .` in older git did not.
Renames are detected, not recorded. An unstaged rename shows as a delete plus an untracked file, which is correct but alarming.
`--porcelain` output is guaranteed stable across git versions; the human format is not. Never parse `git status` without it.
`??` on a file you expected to be tracked usually means it matches a .gitignore rule you forgot. `git check-ignore -v` names the rule.
cheatsheet: the two-column view: X index, Y working tree
staged add / staged delete / deleted on disk only
add the branch and ahead/behind line
